llm.summary: This skill does what it claims, but its default public plain-HTTP API endpoint can expose API keys and uploaded media if users follow the examples or enable the insecure override.

dimensions.detail: Use of KANDINSKY_API_KEY, outbound network access, and local media upload is purpose-aligned, but face images and audio for avatar generation are sensitive and the artifacts do not provide a clear consent/privacy notice beyond general transport warnings.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer, dependency installation, startup hook, tool replacement, or persistence mechanism was found; metadata declares the needed environment variable and curl/python3 requirements.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The docs and code default to http://87.242.117.37:5051 while describing it as private/operator-trusted; the Python client blocks public HTTP by default, but documented curl examples and the allow-insecure override can transmit Bearer credentials and user media over plaintext.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script performs task requests and writes requested outputs only; no privilege escalation, persistent background process, credential-file harvesting, or broad local indexing was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is coherently focused on Kandinsky image, video, upscale, and avatar generation through a remote REST API; reading input media, sending prompts/media, polling tasks, and writing output files are expected for that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you can configure a trusted HTTPS or truly private/loopback Kandinsky endpoint. Do not use the default public HTTP URL or --allow-insecure with real API keys, photos, or voice recordings; use a scoped, revocable key and assume uploaded images/audio are sent to the remote service.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Substantiated in context: the default public HTTP base URL, insecure override, and authorization header on all client requests create real credential/media exposure risk, though no hidden exfiltration or local compromise was found.
[E1] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern because the artifact advertises and demonstrates a plaintext public endpoint for authenticated API calls; this is unsafe even though the Python client warns and blocks it unless overridden.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading supplied images and audio is expected for avatar generation, but the finding is partially accepted because the skill lacks a clear user-facing privacy/consent notice for potentially biometric and voice data.
[LP3] expected: Network, environment-secret, and file-output capabilities fit the stated purpose, but lack of a machine-enforceable least-privilege scope adds review concern when combined with the insecure default endpoint.
[SQP-1] expected: The triggers are broad but still centered on image/video/avatar generation; this is a minor routing/resource-spend concern rather than evidence of hidden behavior.
[AE4] expected: Downgraded: the mixed-script/Unicode signal appears to come from Russian-language documentation and examples, not obfuscation or prompt-injection content.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Russian-only documentation limits usability but does not create a security concern or indicate coercive language behavior.
